<!-- ai-review: failed -->
### AI review: 5 Important finding(s)

The pull request paces the free-running sweep edge in Beats mode, so the playhead moves evenly and audio is placed where it was played. It adds per-sweep placing stamps, lane offset mapping, `PacedEdge::coverShortfall`, a new PacedSweepTests suite and updates to FR-9.2, AD-28 and QS-14. Four specialists reviewed the diff in parallel: correctness, rules, tests and real-time. The real-time specialist found nothing to report. The others reported regressions in `placingStamp` and in the shared delay, and gaps in test coverage.

- **Important** `engine/src/Analyzer.cpp:1299`: placingStamp stops following the host's timeline when the paced delay exceeds about two blocks. The host runs small, jittered blocks, for example 64 to 128 samples at 48 kHz (QS-14 covers 32-sample blocks, jittered). PacedEdge settles on a delay of two or more blocks: the largest lead plus 0.5 ms, decaying only 1% a second (BlockClock.cpp:137). The newest stamp's sampleIndex is newest - blockLength, and the paced edge is at most newest + blockLength - delay. So `latest.sampleIndex <= end` can only hold when delay <= 2*blockLength. With a larger delay the early return `if (placing && latest.sampleIndex > end && ...) return *placing;` fires every time. `placing` then stays at the first stamp after lock, and sweepWindow extrapolates from that stale stamp. A tempo change, loop wrap or relocation never reaches the sweep: the playhead runs past loop points and the cycle length stays at the old tempo. The same happens in every lane through lane.placing. This is a regression from using timeline().latest(), and it contradicts FR-9.2.
  Verification: Timeline::advance sets stamp.sampleIndex to the block start (Timeline.cpp:18), so latest.sampleIndex = newest - blockLen. PacedEdge::edge reaches at most about newest + nextBlockLen - delay. placingStamp returns the stale *placing whenever latest.sampleIndex > end and latest.sampleIndex >= placing->sampleIndex (Analyzer.cpp:1299-1300), so placing advances only if delay <= blockLen + nextBlockLen (about two blocks). forgetPlacing (Analyzer.cpp:487, 492, 1344) fires only on leaving Beats, freezing, a mode switch or having nothing to place, never during steady paced playback. So once the delay exceeds about two blocks, placing keeps the first stamp after the reset, and sweepWindow extrapolates from it: tempo changes, loops and relocations never reach the sweep, for the own track (653), the lanes (1194) and advance. Small jittered blocks or hosts that split one buffer into back-to-back calls reach this. PacedSweepTests uses only 512-sample blocks, where the delay is about one block. The logic is newly added in the diff.
- **Important** `engine/src/Analyzer.cpp:1278`: A lane that stops receiving audio raises the paced delay for every lane to the cap. In Multi or Compare with Beats live, one grouped track stops receiving blocks (the host suspends a silent track, or the track is bypassed) while the others play. That lane's `newest` is fixed while `mapped = own.end + indexOffset` keeps growing. Every placeLanes call (each 2 ms step in advance and each frame) calls coverShortfall(mapped - newest), which sets target = max(target, delay + shortfall). The shortfall grows with real time, so the delay climbs to pacingDelayCapSeconds (0.125 s) and cannot decay while the lane is stalled. The own playhead and all lanes then trail the audio by up to 125 ms instead of about a block, and recover at only 1% a second after the lane resumes. AD-28 states a cost of about a block.
  Verification: Stalled tracks stay in the group: members are removed only when their engine is destroyed (InstanceRegistry.cpp:17), so placeLanes keeps calling laneSweepEdge for them. A stalled lane's newest (Analyzer.cpp:1258) is fixed and its offset stays the same, while own.end advances, so mapped = own.end + indexOffset (1275) grows and coverShortfall(mapped - newest) runs every call (1278-1279). coverShortfall sets target = max(target, delay + samples) (BlockClock.h:128). The delay rises at kRiseRate and reaches the 0.125 s cap (BlockClock.cpp:168-175) after about 1.25 s of stall. It is worse than the finding says: target is lowered only in the decay branch, which runs only when target <= delaySamples (BlockClock.cpp:170-172). Since target is far above the clamped delay, decay never runs, even after the lane resumes, until the own clock restarts (126-132). edge()'s stalled() check (150) looks only at the own clock. coverShortfall is new in the diff, and only a steadily 3 ms late lane is tested.
- **Important** `engine/tests/PacedSweepTests.cpp:431`: Every new test runs at 48 kHz; nothing covers other sample rates or the lane-at-another-rate branch. BeatsHost is built with 48000.0 in every test, and block sizes are only 512 and 2048. laneSweepEdge branches on `rate != own.engine->sampleRate()` (Analyzer.cpp:1260): it resets indexOffset and places the lane at its newest sample. It also does rate-dependent arithmetic: llround(kOffsetToleranceSeconds * rate), sampleIndexAt, and the kMaxSweepSamples clamp, which a 16-bar sweep at 384 kHz exceeds. A Multi group with tracks at 44.1 and 48 kHz (or 48 and 96 kHz) takes the mismatch branch, and no test reaches it. If that branch were dropped, or the tolerance became samples instead of seconds, every test would still pass.
  Verification: laneSweepEdge (pr-head/engine/src/Analyzer.cpp:1260) resets the offset and returns the newest sample when !ownSweepPaced || rate != own.engine->sampleRate(). That branch is reachable only with a paced Beats own sweep, and only PacedSweepTests.cpp sets one up (PacedAnalyzerTests uses Seconds). Every BeatsHost there is built with 48000.0 and prepares every track at that rate, with blocks of 512 or 2048. So the rate mismatch is never true. Deleting that condition, or changing the 1 ms tolerance at 1270 to a fixed 48 samples (identical at 48 kHz), leaves every test passing. This breaks CLAUDE.md Tests (sample rate 44.1 to 384 kHz), .claude/rules/engine.md (test across rates up to 384 kHz) and REVIEW.md (a new failure branch with no test is Important). The change also cites PacedSweepTests as evidence for QS-14, which promises 44.1 to 384 kHz and blocks of 32 to 4096. Caveat: the kMaxSweepSamples clamp predates the change, so that part is weaker.
- **Important** `engine/tests/PacedSweepTests.cpp:763`: New guards in laneSweepEdge and placingStamp have no triggering test: offset persistence, negative mapping and clamp, tempo change, unpaced own sweep with lanes. (a) The persistence branch (Analyzer.cpp:1271, `++lane.offsetDisagreements > kOffsetPersistence`) adopts a new offset after a sustained disagreement, for example after a track's processing restarts and its capture index shifts by 5000 samples. No test changes the offset or makes a transient disagreement come and go. Removing the counter, or never adopting the change, would leave the lane misplaced and pass every test. (b) `std::max(mapped, 0)` and the clamp `std::clamp(edge, min(lane.end, newest), newest)` are never exercised; the tests use only a lane 777 samples ahead. (c) placingStamp's continues() compares tempo, numerator and denominator, but only a position jump at constant tempo is tested. If the tempo comparison were dropped, audio from before the block would be placed at the new tempo unnoticed. (d) The short-sweep test is Single only. In Multi, a sweep under pacedSpanMinimumSeconds makes ownSweepPaced false and lanes use their own newest sample, and that branch is untested.
  Verification: All of these branches are new in the diff: persistence, the negative clamp and the end clamp in laneSweepEdge (diff 248-277), tempo and metre in placingStamp (288-307), and the unpaced early return in ownSweepEdge (222-238). Only PacedSweepTests.cpp exercises them. (a) In BeatsHost each lane's offset is set once in the constructor (55-68), blocks are published at track.offset + track.played (158), and jumpAt (105) changes only the musical position. A disagreement lasts one or two steps, far below kOffsetPersistence = 100, so new-offset adoption never runs: removing the counter, or never adopting a changed offset, passes every test. (b) Multi tests use only offset 777 with the lane late, so std::max(mapped, 0) never acts. (c) Tempo is a constructor constant (42-43, 154) and the metre is never set. A tempo change at a block boundary passes the position check, so dropping the tempo term would go unnoticed. (d) ShowsASweepShorterThanTheMinimumAtTheNewestAudio (283-298) is Single only, and the unpaced lane path is never run in Multi. Note: line 763 is a diff position, not a file line; the file has 397 lines.
- **Important** `engine/tests/PacedSweepTests.cpp:738`: Freeze, display-mode and time-base handling of placing stamps is tested only in Single; Compare is never run. forgetPlacing is called in three places with different own and lane conditions: frozen, Seconds (!synced), switching between Single and Multi, and the no-tempo branch. Only PlacesAudioPlayedDuringAFreezeWhereItWasPlayed exercises one of them (Single, Beats, frozen). A Multi or Compare freeze with a jump, a switch from Multi to Single during a jump, and a Seconds round trip are untested. A wrong lane argument would leave a lane with a stale stamp, and audio played after the jump would show in the wrong columns in Multi with all tests passing. Compare goes through placeLanes, plus lane.image.changes() and the gains and playhead logic in appendComparison, yet the mode loops at lines 626, 650 and 698 cover only kSingle and kMulti.
  Verification: Verified in part. Corrections: the file has 397 lines; the mode loops over {kSingle, kMulti} are at lines 235, 259 and 307. Compare is not an independent gap: it takes the same path as Multi (multi = mode != kSingle, diff 482), and appendComparison is untouched. Seconds is forgotten in produceFrame too; advance() runs only when no frame is wanted (editor/src/FrameFlow.cpp:25). What holds: produceFrame calls forgetPlacing(!synced || isFrozen || multi, !synced || isFrozen || !multi) (diff 136). In Multi, the multi term alone clears ownPlacing. Scenario: play in Single, switch to Multi, the transport loops or relocates, switch back to Single. Without that term, placingStamp would return the stale stamp or placeBefore from the pre-jump position (diff 293-305, 645-650), drawing post-jump audio in the wrong columns. Likewise the isFrozen term in the lanes argument is the only thing that clears lane->placing in a frozen Multi. jumpAt is used only at PacedSweepTests.cpp:316 and :354, the test at :305 never switches modes, and the freeze test at :347 is single-track Single. No other engine test jumps the transport. These are new untested branches the user can reach (REVIEW.md: Important).
- Nit `engine/src/Analyzer.cpp:1257`: The kOffsetPersistence comment ('about 0.2 s') is not true
- Nit `engine/tests/PacedSweepTests.cpp:611`: The lag assertion restates an implementation detail

Fix or answer each Important finding. A maintainer can comment `/ai-review` to review again, or `/ai-review waive <reason>` to pass the check.
This pull request has failed the AI review 3 times; it needs a maintainer's decision, and its author stops fixing findings until then.
